info.title: Ember Data API
info.summary: Programmatic access to Ember's open electricity datasets
info.description:
# Quickstart

## Introduction

An API for curated, consistent energy data.
Ember’s API enables programmatic access to Ember’s electricity datasets.
This guide helps users get started with using the API.

Machine-readable spec: [https://api.ember-energy.org/v1/openapi.json](https://api.ember-energy.org/v1/openapi.json)

## Getting Started

To get set up with the API, follow these steps:

### Register for API key

Sign up for an API key at [https://ember-energy.org/data/api/](https://ember-energy.org/data/api/)

### Documentation

Each endpoint is documented below with an brief explanation, and a link to the
dataset methodology.
Get a feel for the endpoints by clicking "Try it out" in the top right hand corner
of any endpoint.
You then have to add your API key and any parameters you might want to add.
Click Execute to run the query.
The docs will give you a printout of the query you can use outside the docs to
fetch this data (see the Request URL box) as well as the response data that
the API returns (see Response body).
The url outlined in the Request URL box can be used in your desired python,
R, js or other script to fetch data from the API.
Endpoints through CURL are also available.
Congratulations. You are now ready to use Ember’s API

## Examples

### python

``` {python}
import requests

my_api_key = "..."
base_url = "https://api.ember-energy.org"
query_url = (
  f"{base_url}/v1/electricity-generation/yearly"
  + f"?entity_code=BRA&is_aggregate_series=false&start_date=2000&api_key={my_api_key}"
)

response = requests.get(query_url)

if response.status_code == 200:
    data = response.json()

```

### curl

``` {bash}
MY_API_KEY="..."
curl "https://api.ember-energy.org/v1/electricity-generation/yearly?entity_code=BRA&is_aggregate_series=false&start_date=2000&api_key=${MY_API_KEY}"
```

## Endpoint Overview

### Datasets

Dataset endpoints can be used to retrieve data on electricity generation,
power sector emissions and more.
They are available for multiple temporal resolutions (currently yearly and monthly).

### Options

Options endpoints can be used to retrieve possible options to use for
parameters within the dataset endpoints, such as a list of all
countries, regions, fuels within the `/electricity-generation/monthly` endpoint.
The "user_data_range" key within the `stats` object will also show you the
min/max values for the available options.

Options can also be used for finding the available dates within a dataset.
**This can be especially useful in understanding whether new data is available before querying the endpoint.**
Use the `filter_name` of 'date' or 'year'. e.g.
`http://api.ember-energy.org/v1/options/electricity-generation/monthly/date`

## Query parameters

Query parameters with the exception of the api_key are optional.
Parameters can be used to filter the dataset and narrow down the response data.
The parameter names are consistent between datasets,
but can refer to different underlying variables.
For example, in the electricity-generation/yearly dataset,
the entity column refers to “Countries or regions”.
This is highlighted in the swagger docs (https://api.ember-energy.org/v1/docs).

_Note: Parameters like entity, entity_code or series allow multiple values (e.g. entity_code=ARG,DEU,USA)_

### `include_all_dates_value_range`

By default, dataset queries will include the range (min/max) of values in
the response data for any returned metric.
This can be found in the 'stats' object of the returned data.
To also include the range of values for all dates,
rather than just dates selected in the query, set the parameter
`include_all_dates_value_range` to true.
This can be useful when data from a narrower date range needs to be put in
context of the full value range for a metric (e.g. the y-axis of a chart).

### `is_aggregate_series`

Other Renewables generation includes geothermal, tidal and wave generation.
Other Fossil generation includes generation from oil and petroleum products,
as well as manufactured gases and waste.
Head to [Ember's datasets](https://ember-energy.org/data/#datasets)
to view the methodology for each dataset.

## Response Handling

Successful responses will return the response code 200.
Unsuccessful responses will return response codes 400-599, with the most common being:

- 403: Incorrect authentication. Check your API key.
- 404: Incorrect request. Check the URL.

## Rate Limiting

At present, there are no rate limiting restrictions for the API.

## Feedback and Questions

If you have any feedback or questions about our data,
please reach out to us at [data@ember-energy.org](mailto:data@ember-energy.org).

## License and Attribution

Our data is published using the CC-BY-4.0 license.
Anyone is able to use our data for any purpose (personal, commercial, etc.).
The only requirements by this license are that:

1. Ember is cited as the data source.
E.g. 'Monthly electricity generation data, Ember'
2. You may not add any additional legal/technological restrictions to the data.

Additional details on the terms of the license can be found at:

get.description:
Get grid carbon intensity data at a yearly grain.
    e.g.

`https://api.ember-energy.org/v1/carbon-intensity/yearly?entity_code=AFG,BRA,DEU,ZAF&start_date=2020&api_key=MY_API_KEY`
    

The methodology of this dataset can be found on its [dataset page](https://ember-energy.org/data/yearly-electricity-data/)
    within the 'Methodology - Ember Electricity Data' pdf.

get.description:
Get installed wind and solar capacity in a monthly grain.
    e.g.

`https://api.ember-energy.org/v1/installed-capacity/monthly?is_aggregate_entity=false&series=Solar,Wind&start_date=2020-01&api_key=MY_API_KEY`
    

The methodology of this dataset can be found on its [dataset page](https://ember-energy.org/data/monthly-wind-and-solar-capacity-data/)
    within the 'Methodology - Monthly Wind and Solar Capacity Data' pdf.

parameters.name: entity

schema.description: (Optional) [List of comma separated] country[s] or region[s] to return data for. Use the `options` endpoint to find the acceptable values. Note: some countries have a comma in their name. The comma can be escaped with a backslash (\\) to avoid being treated as a list of two countries. e.g.`entity=Saint Helena\, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha,Saint Kitts and Nevis`queries the two entities `Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha` and `Saint Kitts and Nevis`.
schema.title: Entity
